papers.title: WaveGen: Truly End-to-End Waveform Generation via Internal Spectral Trajectory Learning
papers.abstract: This work proposes WaveGen, a fully end-to-end diffusion-based text-to-waveform framework based on Spectral Forcing, which jointly learns an internal spectral trajectory and the target waveform trajectory within a single model, enabling direct end-to-end text-to-waveform generation. papers.title: TTSonic: A Unified Framework for Composable and Controllable Speech Generation
papers.abstract: Modern text-to-speech (TTS) systems can synthesize natural and expressive speech, yet a practical speech foundation model must go beyond naturalness to offer stable quality, precise controllability, and a broad set of composable capabilities within a unified framework. We present TTSonic, a unified speech generation model that supports zero-shot TTS, voice cloning, prosody cloning, instruction following, voice conversion, and cloning from noisy reference speech. papers.title: Adaptive Fisher-Whitened Cross-Covariance for Low-Resource Speech Recognition
papers.abstract: Adapting multilingual speech foundation models to low-resource languages remains difficult, especially for languages that are poorly represented during pre-training. While parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) reduces the cost of adapting large models, conventional approaches such as LoRA rely on generic low-rank parameterizations and do not explicitly use downstream task information to define the adaptation subspace. papers.abstract: We present M5-TTS, a compact text-to-speech system supporting multilingual and Chinese multidialect synthesis, zero-shot voice cloning, speaker-specific multilingual generation, and CPU streaming. papers.title: Speech Tokenizers are Vulnerable: Transferable Semantic Attack and Robust Tokenizer
papers.abstract: Speech tokenizers serve as speech front ends, encoding input speech signals into representations for downstream models, such as automatic speech recognition (ASR) systems and large audio-language models (LALMs). In this paper, we find that speech tokenizers are fragile at the semantic level: small perturbations can disrupt their semantic encoding process and consequently cause severe degradation in downstream ASR and LALM performance. papers.title: Alania-2: Turkish text-to-speech with instant and fine-tuned voice cloning
papers.abstract: We present Alania-2, a Turkish text-to-speech (TTS) system with two built-in voices, voice design from text descriptions, and two kinds of voice cloning. papers.title: MineralExp: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Experimental Design in Real-World Mineral Exploration
papers.abstract: In mineral exploration, verifying geological hypotheses relies on designing a variety of geochemical experiments. While large language model (LLM) agents increasingly automate downstream geoscientific data analysis, a crucial upstream capability remains largely unexplored: automated geochemical experimental design, i.e., deciding which experiments to conduct before committing to costly laboratory work. papers.abstract: Cameroon Pidgin English (a West African Pidgin English variety) and Camfranglais are widely used in Cameroon, yet to our knowledge, neither has a dedicated spoken Natural Language Inference (NLI) resource. We introduce CamSpokenNLI, a pilot dataset of 114 scenario-matched spoken NLI items in each variety (228 in total), recorded by one native speaker from Buea. papers.abstract: Full-duplex spoken dialogue, in which a system listens while it speaks and can backchannel, yield the floor, and be interrupted, is usually obtained by training on hundreds of thousands to millions of hours of speech. papers.abstract: Streaming speech recognizers output a word only after the speaker has finished it, typically 90-400 ms later. papers.abstract: Diarization-conditioned target-speaker ASR (TS-ASR), in particular Diarization-conditioned Whisper (DiCoW), is an accurate and data-efficient approach to multi-talker transcription. papers.abstract: We introduce Gamer, a generalist agent framework built for long-horizon tasks in complex interactive environments. Its end-to-end architecture combines perception, memory management, and multi-step reasoning. A shared training and deployment pipeline supports interaction with both conventional 2D graphical interfaces and complex 3D simulated worlds. papers.title: Envisioning Agentic Robotics: A New Era of Robotic Systems
papers.abstract: The release of GPT-6 Astra marks the emergence of a new paradigm in robotics: agentic robotics. Within weeks, frontier models with agentic harnesses matched or exceeded task-specific policies on many embodied benchmarks. Instead of training a dedicated policy for each family of tasks, an agentic robotic system applies a foundation model to open-world embodied tasks. papers.abstract: Speech applications require decisions about term presence, turn completion, and language within an audio window. papers.abstract: General-purpose state-of-the-art automatic speech recognition (ASR) systems fail systematically for speakers with moderate to severe speech disabilities. papers.abstract: Text-to-speech systems built from a language model and a flow-matching mel decoder now run the decoder with two to four Euler steps instead of the official ten or more. papers.abstract: Perceptual audio codecs often use predictive coding to further reduce signal redundancy. papers.abstract: We present Walrus, a unified 8B speech-and-audio foundation model handling speech recognition (including code-switching and multi-talker speech), speech-to-text and speech-to-speech translation, text-to-speech, emotion recognition, audio captioning, and general audio understanding. papers.abstract: Music audio generation spans instrumental clips, full songs with vocals, edits of existing recordings, and systems that play alongside a musician in real time. This monograph explains the methods behind these systems for readers familiar with neural-network training who are new to music generation. papers.abstract: Nepali speakers regularly mix English words into conversation, but multilingual speech recognisers often struggle with language switches and the writing script used for English words. papers.abstract: Recent advances in Speech Language Models (SpeechLMs), which integrate large language models with speech foundation models, have enabled unified sequence modeling of speech processing tasks. papers.abstract: Automatic speech recognition models suffer from catastrophic forgetting when adapted to new domains, accents, or downstream tasks. papers.abstract: In Taiwanese Hokkien automatic speech recognition (ASR), prior studies often treat tone sandhi as a major challenge under the assumption that models fail to process implicit phonological variations. papers.title: Enhancing Language Model Reasoning with Structured Multi-Level Modeling
papers.abstract: Inference-time scaling enhances a model's reasoning by extending its chain-of-thought (CoT). papers.title: JFinBench: A Continuously Refreshable Japanese Financial Benchmark from the Latest Certification Exams
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly applied to finance, creating a need for benchmarks that evaluate their capabilities across financial systems with different regulations and practices. However, existing financial benchmarks provide limited coverage of country-specific financial systems, and they are difficult to keep up to date as released questions leak into training data. We introduce JFinBench, a Japanese financial benchmark comprising 321 examples from the 2026 editions of six regularly administered certification exams covering accounting, tax, financial planning, and banking.

papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used by reviewers to highlight weaknesses during the reviewing process, and their outputs often shape the reviews that humans submit. papers.abstract: In this report, we introduce the Reciprocal World Model (RWM) and present Duo v1, a full-duplex world model that continuously perceives audiovisual inputs while responding to users in real time. papers.abstract: Mechanistic Interpretability (MI) has made significant progress in explaining the internal computations of Large Language Models (LLMs); however, these advances have yet to demonstrate comparable success in explaining the decision-making processes of LLM-based agents. papers.abstract: Web agents powered by large language and vision-language models are increasingly applied to realistic browser work that spans heterogeneous applications, multimodal content, and stateful workflows. papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) typically relies on a verifier that can reliably judge whether sampled solutions are correct. papers.title: ZONOS3-Mini Technical Report
papers.abstract: ZONOS3-Mini is an ultra-compact, ultra-fast, zero-shot voice-cloning TTS model. The model can run in real time on a laptop or smartphone. papers.abstract: Can a speech generator also serve as an effective voice encoder? papers.abstract: As modern text-to-speech systems become increasingly intelligible and natural, evaluation is shifting from detecting gross synthesis failures to identifying subtle departures from lifelike human delivery. We propose JEV-VAD, an ASR-free framework that combines task-first conditioning, a scalar endpoint readout, and decoder-prefix pruning. papers.title: Cross-Codec Robustness in Speech Watermarking
papers.abstract: Generative speech models synthesize audio that is difficult to distinguish from human recordings. papers.abstract: Audio language models are meant to answer questions from the audio itself, but an hour-long recording rarely fits in their context, and the answer often depends on a few seconds of it. papers.abstract: Abstract Aims With the rapid growth of cardiac implantable electronic device (CIED) implantations, lead management has become increasingly challenging. papers.abstract: Large language models have made rapid progress in agentic reasoning and tool use, raising expectations for agents that can take over realistic productivity work from humans. papers.abstract: Running large language models (LLMs) on local devices keeps data private, removes per-token cost, cuts network latency, and keeps working without a connection. papers.abstract: Self-supervised speech models (S3Ms) have been scaled up to thousands of languages and millions of hours of audio, yet little is known about how these models structure semantic knowledge across languages. papers.abstract: Multimodal continual instruction tuning requires multimodal large language models to sequentially acquire new capabilities without catastrophic forgetting. papers.abstract: Test-time scaling of diffusion models with sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) has become a promising strategy for sampling under user-specified rewards, such as human preference scores. papers.abstract: Agentic reinforcement learning (RL) increasingly relies on a harness, the scaffold around the model that decides what it sees of its own interaction and what guidance it receives. papers.abstract: This paper introduces MeReader, a privacy-preserving, offline and progress-aware AI assistant designed to function as a contextual companion for narrative reading on consumer hardware. papers.abstract: Program induction refers to the process in which a learner aims to recover a program from a few given input-output examples. papers.abstract: LLM-based verifiers are increasingly used to evaluate agent executions, but their reliability is typically measured under a single representation of the trajectory. papers.title: FEND: Far-End Detection in Outbound Voice AI Calls
papers.abstract: When a conversational Voice AI agent places an outbound call, the far end may be a live person, a voicemail greeting, an interactive voice response (IVR) system, or increasingly another AI system answering on the callee's behalf. papers.abstract: Can you trust a finance agent you did not build? papers.abstract: Multi-agent systems solve complex tasks by decomposing them into subtasks, delegating the subtasks to agents, and aggregating the agents' responses using an aggregation rule. papers.abstract: Typhoon is an audiovisual installation based on Joseph Conrad's novella, in which Captain MacWhirr steers the steamer Nan-Shan directly into and through a catastrophic storm. papers.abstract: Audio phase relations encode source locations, yet existing large audio-language models (LALM) reduce audio to single-channel content to stabilise general audio understanding, leaving spatial information for direction, distance, and source-relation questions unused. papers.abstract: Spatial hearing in multi-receiver environments requires identifying who speaks, where they are, and how they move. papers.abstract: Recent music foundation models have achieved remarkable progress in music representation learning, yet most existing approaches rely on Transformer architectures whose quadratic attention complexity introduces substantial computational and memory overhead when modeling long-duration music recordings. papers.abstract: Large audio-language models (LALMs) typically encode audio once and conduct subsequent multi-step reasoning in a language-dominated space, weakening access to fine-grained acoustic evidence. papers.abstract: Natural-language audio editing requires connecting a user's intent to specific sounds and time regions while preserving surrounding content. papers.abstract: Spoken Language Diarization (SLD) models provide frame-level language information of a speech recording. papers.abstract: The performance of speech classification systems such as speech emotion recognition or pathological speech detection can degrade substantially when there is a domain shift between training and test data. papers.abstract: Recent work shows that multimodal agents increasingly self-improve without recurring human annotation. papers.abstract: While multimodal agents now carry out complex data analysis with tools, their ability to turn decades of satellite imagery into reliable land-change analysis, crucial for Earth observation science, remains unmeasured. papers.abstract: Common data elements (CDEs) support clinical data comparability but are usually defined manually. papers.abstract: Listeners can judge an agent's speech on how human it sounds (human-likeness) and on how much they would want to talk to it (conversational preference). papers.abstract: Modern discrete neural audio codecs facilitate speech synthesis by replacing continuous acoustic representations with low-frame-rate discrete token sequences. papers.abstract: Neural audio codecs are increasingly used for low-bitrate speech coding and serve as tokenizers for speech language models, yet it remains unclear how their codebook hierarchies encode speaker traits and speech characteristics. papers.abstract: Real-time voice agents have moved from research prototypes to production deployments, yet the literature describing them is fragmented across three communities that rarely cite one another: speech foundation modelling, turn-taking psycholinguistics, and agentic evaluation. papers.abstract: We present FoleyForge, a generative model for instruction-based editing of sound effects. papers.abstract: Large Audio Language Models (LALMs) enable generative reasoning over complex acoustic scenes but often exhibit prediction instability. papers.abstract: Autonomous crystal-structure determination from powder X-ray diffraction (pXRD) remains a key bottleneck for self-driving materials laboratories. We formulate the task of pXRD structure determination as a verifiable agentic search problem: candidate structures can be assessed during inference through forward-simulated profile agreement and during evaluation through structural matching to a known reference. papers.abstract: Inference-time scaling is often treated as a token-budget problem, but a failed coding agent can seek qualitatively different resources: computation, information, or feedback. papers.abstract: Best-of-N sampling is a simple inference-time scaling strategy for large language models, yet its behavior under incomplete reward models remains poorly understood. papers.abstract: Autonomous agents modify prompts, memories, tools, workflows, and policies using interaction histories. papers.abstract: Speculative decoding accelerates generation by letting a lightweight drafter propose tokens for parallel verification by a target model. papers.abstract: Previous work has shown that alignment training on individual LLM agents can fail to transfer to multi-agent settings. papers.abstract: Agentic workflows enable AI agents to perform recurring repository tasks on schedules or in response to repository events. papers.abstract: Foundation models trained on large unlabeled corpora develop emergent capabilities, tasks that go beyond the training objective. papers.abstract: Self-evolving agents improve their own skills, memory, and harness code from experience without retraining the base LLM, and group-evolving agents go further by sharing these lessons across agents. papers.abstract: Generalist manipulation policies can benefit from the complementary experience of humans, real robots, and simulated agents. papers.abstract: How multimodal language models should encode visual input remains up for debate. papers.abstract: GPT-6 Astra can drive a robot arm directly through a fixed harness, and scores of such robot-use agents on RoboDojo have risen quickly since. papers.abstract: Self-improving embodied agents are increasingly being developed and compared on robot simulation benchmarks. papers.abstract: While search agents demonstrate impressive capabilities in multi-step question answering, their robustness to poor-quality evidence remains under-explored. papers.abstract: Tool timeouts can leave AI agents facing ambiguous tool outcomes and partial execution: an action may have failed, committed or remained in flight while other workflow steps have already completed. papers.abstract: Second-order optimizers (e.g., Shampoo, SOAP) have emerged as compelling alternatives to Adam/AdamW and promise faster per-step convergence than AdamW in transformer training. papers.title: PhysLoop: Harnessing LLMs' Physics Awareness for Self-Improving Video Generation Models
papers.abstract: Video generation models produce visually realistic videos but still struggle with physical dynamics and causal consistency. papers.abstract: Subliminal learning is a phenomenon in large language models (LLMs) where a teacher passes a hidden preference to a student through training data unrelated to that preference. papers.abstract: AI agents deployed on the open web are becoming more capable of performing actions that may breach contractual provisions and violate computer security laws. papers.abstract: Web-facing AI agents repeatedly access webpages, documents, repositories, and tool responses, yet reading interfaces often expose entire objects when only sparse evidence is needed. papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) draw on parametric knowledge and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) to solve knowledge-intensive tasks. papers.title: A Multi-Layered AI Pipeline for BPMN Generation from Natural Language
papers.abstract: The automated transformation of unstructured natural language process descriptions into Business Process Model and Notation (BPMN) diagrams remains a challenging task, due to linguistic ambiguity and the difficulty to detect non-adjacent control-flow relationships. This paper proposes a solution for generating BPMN models from natural language descriptions through a multi-layered pipeline that integrates transformer-based architectures, Large Language Models and ontology population. papers.abstract: The hidden layers of Large Language Models (LLMs) are believed to encode representations of the data whose abstraction increases with depth. However, in the absence of an operational notion of abstraction, this statement is hard to test quantitatively. papers.title: Agent-as-a-Judge
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence has progressed from task-specific systems toward general models spanning perception, generation, reasoning, and autonomous interaction, making reliable evaluation essential for comparison, deployment, and post-training feedback. papers.title: AmbiSteer: Selectively Eliciting Ambiguity-Aware Responses in Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) often exhibit overconfidence, providing firm answers even when visual evidence is insufficient. A prominent case is referential ambiguity in Visual Question Answering (VQA), where multiple entities in an image are plausible referents of a question. papers.title: CarryOn: Learning What to Keep in Context for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
papers.abstract: Long-horizon LLM agents can coordinate tools and applications to complete complex, multi-step tasks. As their interaction histories grow, effective context management becomes essential for reliable and efficient execution. Existing methods reduce context through summarization, pruning, or history selection. papers.title: RAG-FGO: Dynamic Optimization of Query-Rewriting Agents for Generative RAG
papers.abstract: In retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), query rewriting serves as a core interface that aligns user intent with external knowledge bases, and its effectiveness directly determines overall system performance. However, generative retrieval faces three critical challenges in real-world deployment: noisy retrieval feedback, the difficulty of jointly optimizing discrete prompt templates and continuous decoding-control parameters, and the limited generalization of static rewriting strategies under semantically complex scenarios. papers.title: LuthorSQL: A One-Pass Text-to-SQL Model as System 1 for a Slower LLM Agent
papers.abstract: Frontier LLM agents that query databases with tools are among the most accurate text-to-SQL systems, but per-query calls to a hosted model are slow, costly, and expose sensitive organizational queries to external APIs. For example, a Claude Opus 5.5 agent serving 10,000 queries a day costs over $70,000 a year at list price. To what extent can local hardware already owned by an organization offload this burden without compromising the agent's accuracy? papers.title: GDP.xlsx: Benchmarking Frontier Models on Professional Workbooks
papers.abstract: We introduce GDP_xlsx, a benchmark of 70 realistic workplace requests written by professionals in 13 domains, each paired with an expert rubric of binary criteria and with the complete workbook or CSV file it refers to. Together the files hold 2.18 million populated cells, and the rubrics 791 criteria. Agents work in a container with spreadsheet tools, and an agentic judge that can open the file applies the rubric. papers.abstract: Policy gradient methods are widely used to align large language model outputs with human preferences, but the log-likelihoods they require cannot be directly computed in Masked Diffusion Language Models (MDLMs). papers.title: What LLM Agents See and What Users Say
papers.abstract: Before an LLM agent cancels a reservation or deletes a folder for a user, what stops it from acting on a false assumption: what its tools show, or what the user says? In this work, we study this gap with presupposition theory from linguistics: an agent may act only if each claim behind the act (e.g., one reservation fits the name) is seen to hold, answered by the user, or disclosed while the act can be undone. papers.abstract: Evaluations of multi-agent language models often compare communicating architectures against a single greedy pass. This practice confounds coordination with sample multiplicity and inference compute. We synthesize nine primary empirical evaluations comprising 516 unique multi-agent configurations organized along a resource vector R with six dimensions and a baseline ladder with four categories. papers.title: LightTAR: Light and Fast Target-Aware Representations for Multimodal Tabular Learning
papers.abstract: Multimodal tabular learning involves classification and regression on tables combining structured numerical and categorical features with unstructured text and images. These unstructured fields are commonly represented by pretrained encoder embeddings reduced with principal component analysis (PCA). papers.title: AI-Voyager: A Public-Interest System for Human-AI Civic Reasoning to Contest and Shape the Rules That Govern AI
papers.abstract: Governments are writing rules for artificial intelligence that decide what counts as an automated decision or a harm, often before the people they affect have a chance to question them. We introduce AI-Voyager, a public-interest system for human-AI civic reasoning, in which people and AI work together to understand, contest and shape the rules that govern AI. papers.abstract: Can sustained gain-loss (valence) framing sway an LLM agent toward market manipulation? papers.title: Tracing Knowledge and Reasoning in LLM
papers.abstract: Current evaluations of Large Language Models (LLMs) report performance at the dataset or task level, revealing what a model achieves but offering little insight into the internal processing associated with its performance. We propose a task-centric framework for characterising the model-internal processing elicited by a benchmark. papers.title: Unfinished-Bench: Measuring Rule Violations by Persistent Agents in Realistic Work Environments
papers.abstract: AI agents are increasingly equipped with persistence toward task completion to run delegated work autonomously for long periods, under many unstated constraints from internal documents and other people's authority. When completion requires violating a rule, the agent must decide alone, yet benchmarks of instruction-rule conflicts state the rule in the prompt or keep it hidden and do not evaluate persistence. papers.title: CoReMem: Cost-Internalizing Memory for Successive Coding Tasks with Prospective Valuation
papers.abstract: Coding agents tackle successive tasks on an evolving repository, carrying forward edits and writing memory before the next task is known. Selecting memory for unknown next tasks requires balancing future usefulness against the costs of writing and reading it. The actor must also decide when acting on available memory saves effort as the task unfolds. papers.abstract: On-device inference requires kernels that make effective use of local accelerators. Efficient training and evaluation of models that generate Apple Metal kernels benefit from native macOS tools and concurrent agent sessions. These sessions alternate between model requests, development commands, and GPU execution, leaving GPU capacity idle for much of a rollout. papers.abstract: A small fine-tuned parser that emits a well-formed but wrong tree fails silently: nothing downstream can tell. papers.title: Parameter-Efficient Conciseness Adaptation: Differentiable Length Control for Concise Clinical Reasoning in Smaller Language Models
papers.abstract: Smaller language models (SLMs) make it feasible to deploy clinical natural language processing where large proprietary models are too costly, and parameter-efficient fine-tuning allows them to be specialised on commodity hardware. One obstacle persists after training: on medical tasks these models answer at far greater length than the clinical question requires. papers.abstract: Enforcement defenses against prompt injection, such as CaMeL, Progent, IPIGuard and DRIFT, ask the agent's own model to write a security artifact (a program, a privilege policy, a dependency graph or a constraint list) that code then enforces. papers.abstract: Program evolution provides a promising approach to discover agent memory designs and study the choices underlying their effectiveness. We introduce MAPE, a framework that evolves whole memory programs from minimal seeds through a standardized lifecycle interface and an iterative diagnosis-proposal loop. papers.title: Evaluating Pretrained Language Semantics for Structured EHR Prediction Tasks
papers.abstract: Structured Electronic Health Records (EHR) models typically treat each clinical concept as a dataset-specific token, discarding the natural-language semantics associated with the event. As a result, relationships between concepts must largely be learned from EHR co-occurrence, without directly exploiting any prior semantic knowledge. papers.title: CoTTAGE: An Explainable Judge for Text-to-Audio Generation
papers.abstract: Rapid progress in text-to-audio (TTA) generation demands reliable and explainable automatic evaluation. However, existing metrics fail to simultaneously deliver high correlation with human judgments and meaningful, audio-grounded explanations, forcing reliance on labor-intensive human evaluation that bottlenecks model development iteration. papers.abstract: Low-resource, agglutinative languages challenge low-latency ASR, as fixed lookahead windows fail when grapheme order diverges, suffixes cross code-switch boundaries, or code-switching data is imbalanced. papers.title: MusicFlux: Flexible Conditioning for Text-Guided Music Generation and Editing
authors: Leonardo Boulitreau de Menezes Martins Marques
papers.abstract: Music editing transforms existing recordings while preserving their original attributes. papers.abstract: We present Textraction, a text-guided speaker extraction framework that enables the selective extraction of desired speakers or noise sources from an audio mixture using only natural-language descriptions. papers.abstract: The rapid progress of generative speech models has made high-fidelity voice cloning and editing cheap, fast, and widely accessible, weakening the security of voiceprint-based authentication in mobile speech interactions. papers.abstract: Describing hours of audio requires accurate event timing and sustained descriptive detail throughout the recording. papers.abstract: Multimodal LLMs have made remarkable progress in perceiving the physical world, while their perceptual scope remains largely human-centric, focusing on what humans can directly see or hear. This progress raises the prospect of perception beyond human limits, such as extending hearing to sounds that are inaudible to humans. papers.abstract: Recent audio embedding models learn representations that transfer across clip- and frame-level tasks, yet they operate almost exclusively on single-channel signals and are blind to spatial structure. papers.title: SAS: Scene-Annotated AudioSet Strong for Joint Scene-Event Analysis
papers.abstract: Context is central to human auditory perception, as listeners interpret sounds within their acoustic environment to resolve ambiguity. However, large-scale datasets that jointly capture sound events and acoustic scenes remain limited. papers.abstract: Demonstrations are an effective way to accelerate single-agent reinforcement learning (RL), but extending this idea to multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) is non-trivial as it is difficult and often impossible for a single person to teleoperate multiple agents simultaneously. papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) agents are expected to complete tasks while following rules of conduct, but these objectives can conflict. We study how evolutionary selection shapes an agent's choices between them, and whether experience can make those choices reflect human judgments and withstand subsequent pressures. papers.abstract: Autonomous trading agents need controls that prevent problematic orders without making legitimate tasks impractical. papers.abstract: AI-enabled remote patient monitoring is evolving beyond passive data collection toward agentic AI systems that interpret patient states, coordinate care, and initiate action across domestic and clinical settings. This structured scoping review finds that mature agentic care has not yet emerged: Most systems remain human led, while stronger decision-action coupling and embodied AI remain largely confined to prototypes and pilots. papers.abstract: Clinical world models expose language-model agents to predicted patient responses, but simulations can be unreliable for poorly supported treatments or unfamiliar hospitals. papers.abstract: Reliable use of large language models (LLMs) requires uncertainty estimates that separate ambiguity intrinsic to a prompt from genuine knowledge gaps. papers.abstract: AI-enabled smart homes are becoming more common across the grid edge. However, there has not been much work on failure response. papers.abstract: Accessible mobility is user-conditioned rather than scene-intrinsic, as walkable paths for one embodiment are inaccessible to another. papers.abstract: Web platforms record user and item activity in relational databases whose schemas differ from platform to platform, which makes it difficult to transfer predictive models between them. Relational foundation models address this through cross-database pretraining, yet recent improvements have relied on increasingly large pretraining corpora. papers.abstract: Coding agents increasingly review code, yet whether they catch the privacy defects that laws such as the GDPR require software to avoid remains largely untested, partly because few datasets connect real privacy defects to their accepted fixes and review context. papers.abstract: Activation steering via sparse autoencoders (SAEs) enables behavioral control of large language models without task-specific fine-tuning. papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) generate text one token at a time, yet how a particular generation relates to the geometry learned in pre-training remains unclear. papers.abstract: Personal assistant robots powered by large language models (LLMs) are likely to enter everyday life within the next decade, but the values that should guide their behaviour remain largely unspecified. papers.abstract: Differential association theory and its extension, social learning theory, hold that rule-breaking, and the definitions that make it acceptable, are learned through interaction with others. papers.abstract: Direct image-to-video diffusion models entangle pixel synthesis with implicit latent motion, precluding persistent 3D mechanical equilibrium, mid-rollout intervention, and counterfactual force control. papers.abstract: Embedded audio agents need a nearby edge server for speed, but a server-dependent agent returns nothing when the link fails. papers.abstract: Chinese Grammatical Error Correction (CGEC) is typically formulated as a text-to-text problem. papers.abstract: In many long-horizon settings, an agent's own choices create future constraints: committing finite capacity establishes future obligations and forecloses later opportunities. papers.abstract: Scientific literature search can benefit from locally deployed LLM assistants, which reduce reliance on hosted model providers while giving research teams greater control over their data and infrastructure. papers.abstract: Scaling laws indicate that the generalization error of a large language model (LLM) decreases monotonically with model size once data is sufficient, and the corollary that larger models outperform smaller ones is now widely accepted. papers.abstract: Cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) supports coordinated decision-making in distributed Web services, multi-robot control, and collaborative games through learned coordination conventions. papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics (ST) prediction from histology aims to infer spatially resolved gene expression profiles directly from tissue images. This is a challenging problem that is currently often addressed with complicated model architectures, additional inputs, and complicated training procedures, while remaining limited to fixed, small gene panels. papers.abstract: LLM agents that execute multi-step tool calls must satisfy two objectives simultaneously: completing the user's task (utility) and conforming to domain policies and correctness constraints (safety). papers.abstract: We propose structured speaker conditioning (SSC) for diarization-guided target-speaker recognition. papers.abstract: End-to-end ASR systems must jointly solve speech- text alignment and token prediction from sequence-level super- vision. papers.abstract: BEST-RQ, based on random projection and quantization, has been a well-established self-supervised learning approach to learn speech representations from large-scale unlabeled audio due to its high performance and efficiency. papers.abstract: Despite recent advances in neural speech codecs, achieving highfidelity speech reconstruction at low bitrates remains a formidable challenge. papers.abstract: Existing instruction-based TTS systems primarily support one-shot, utterance-level control, where a single instruction determines the speaking style of an entire utterance. papers.abstract: Cascaded spoken dialogue systems comprise perception-and-comprehension, decision-making, and response-generation modules. papers.abstract: Objective: This review aims to provide a comprehensive synthesis of domain adaptation (DA) and domain general- ization (DG) strategies for AD detection. papers.abstract: Extended reality (XR) enables controlled yet naturalistic multisensory experiments, but its validity depends on whether virtualized cues are perceptually plausible and lead to behavior comparable to the real world. papers.abstract: Perceptual evaluation of generated music is essential for developing text-to-music (TTM) generation systems. papers.abstract: Lyric intelligibility significantly impacts music engagement and comprehension, especially for hearing-impaired individuals. papers.abstract: With the growing need for evaluating Large Language Models (LLMs) and their applications to speech, challenges persist in summarizing and evaluating conversations that lack a clear end goal. papers.abstract: Microphones let an autonomous vehicle sense into areas its cameras and LiDAR cannot see, by picking up the sound that other traffic participants emit. papers.abstract: We introduce AudioCodex, a fully causal autoencoder for live generative audio applications that compresses stereo audio into compact continuous latent sequences at ~10 Hz. papers.abstract: Recent progress on contrastive audio-language models can be attributed mainly to the scale and quality of their training data. papers.title: Music Inpainting With Similarity-Guided Latent Diffusion
papers.abstract: We propose a music inpainting technique combining similarity matching and a diffusion-based generative model to replace large segments of audio recordings with suitable alternatives. papers.title: CallCleaner: Lightweight Bioacoustic Denoising from an Audio Foundation Model
papers.abstract: Many studies of animal vocalizations require clean recordings, but animals are usually recorded in the field, with background noise from weather, vehicles, and other animals. papers.abstract: Existing beat-tracking benchmarks draw from a narrow range of musical cultures, predominantly Western, and are difficult to scale due to reliance on expert annotation. papers.abstract: Antarctic whale vocalization detection requires temporally localizing call boundaries in long underwater recordings and classifying them into predefined call types. papers.abstract: Large public datasets have driven recent progress in machine learning, from text and vision to speech and general audio. papers.abstract: Speech retrieval finds relevant spoken documents given a spoken query. papers.title: MEM-SQL: Memory-Empowered Text-to-SQL
papers.abstract: Text-to-SQL systems translate natural language questions into SQL queries over increasingly complex databases. We introduce HARE (History-AwaRe Text-to-SQL BEnchmark) to measure the accuracy and cost of adapting historical SQL. papers.title: HALO: Human-Aligned Data Collection for WhoLe-body MObile Manipulation
papers.abstract: Learning whole-body mobile manipulation requires demonstrations that coordinate bimanual actions with locomotion across extended workspaces. papers.abstract: Frontier video generation models work in a VAE latent space that compresses video in both space and time. papers.abstract: Medical imaging is essential for diagnosing disease, guiding treatment and monitoring patients over time. papers.abstract: AI "humanizers" rewrite machine-generated text so that detectors classify it as human-written. papers.abstract: System One models promise fast, general-purpose decision-making without lengthy token generation. papers.title: BirdDreams: Joint Perspective and BEV Video Generation for a Plausible, Reactive Driving World Model
papers.abstract: Driving world models aim to simulate how a scene unfolds under different ego actions. papers.abstract: LiDAR point clouds and 3D semantic occupancy represent two distinct modalities capturing fine-grained metric geometry and dense volumetric semantics, respectively, holding natural potential for mutual complementarity. papers.abstract: Industry now relies on LLMs to write a large share of production code. papers.abstract: Human Label Variation (HLV) is increasingly recognised as an informative signal that reflects meaningful differences in how people interpret the same input. papers.abstract: Evaluating grammatical knowledge in language models requires benchmarks that cover diverse linguistic phenomena and are validated against human judgments. papers.abstract: As AI conference submissions grow rapidly, AI reviewers are being considered as an alternative.
